MessageExchange.name: AfsCheck
MessageExchange.Description: Generate a CRC checksum from the contents a file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns the CRC of the data from the specified file starting at the specified offset.
This is the CRC according to the CRC16-CCITT standard using the polynomial 0x1021 and an initial seed of 0xFFFF. The most significant byte is returned first.

Revision.name: AfsCheckV1
Revision.Description: Generate a CRC checksum from the contents of a file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsCheckFile
MessageExchange.Description: Generate a CRC checksum from the contents of the open file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns the CRC of the data from the file currently opended by AfsOpenFile at the specified offset.
This is the CRC according to the CRC16-CCITT standard using the polynomial 0x1021 and an initial seed of 0xFFFF. The most significant byte is returned first.
Attempting to check a file not open in read mode will cause an exception.
This command is deprecated in favor of the atomic file access command AfsCheck.

Revision.name: AfsCheckFileV1
Revision.Description: Generate a CRC checksum from the contents of the open file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsClearBleFaultLog
MessageExchange.Description: Clear the BLE fault log file by writing zeros
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command writes zeros to the start of the BLE fault log to invalidate it (it does not erase the entire file contents).
The offset field should be set to its default value of zero.

Revision.name: AfsClearBleFaultLogV1
Revision.Description: Clear the BLE fault log file by writing zeros (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsClearExceptionTrace
MessageExchange.Description: Clear the exception trace file by writing zeros
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command writes zeros to the start of the exception trace file to invalidate it (it does not erase the entire file contents).
The offset field should be set to its default value of zero.

Revision.name: AfsClearExceptionTraceV1
Revision.Description: Clear the exception trace file by writing zeros (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsCloseFile
MessageExchange.Description: Close the open file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command closes the current file.
Attempting to close a file when one is not open will be ignored.
This command is deprecated in favor of the atomic file access commands (AfsGetAttributes, AfsRead, AfsWrite and AfsCheck).

Revision.name: AfsCloseFileV1
Revision.Description: Close the open file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsErase
MessageExchange.Description: Erase a file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command erases bytes in the specified file starting at the specified offset. Any part of the file can be erased and there are no alignment restrictions.
Erased bytes are set to 0xFF.

Revision.name: AfsEraseV1
Revision.Description: Erase a file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsEraseExceptionLog
MessageExchange.Description: Erase all records from the exception log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command clears all exceptions from the exception log file. It is safe to execute this command at any time because it is only updated during system initialization.
All log file flags are currently reserved. Set the Flags field to zero.

Revision.name: AfsEraseExceptionLogV1
Revision.Description: Erase all records from the exception log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsEraseLog
MessageExchange.Description: Erase all records from a log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command erases all records data from the specified log file (makes it empty).
All log file flags are currently reserved. Set the Flags field to zero.
This command should not be used for log files that are updated during normal operation unless the aid is in factory mode, otherwise the log file may become corrupted.

Revision.name: AfsEraseLogV1
Revision.Description: Erase all records from a log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsFileChanged
MessageExchange.Description: File changed
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
An event is generated when a file that was opened in write mode is closed (which means the data has been committed to NVM).
AFS internal operations on a file (for example to maintain backup copies of a failsafe file) are excluded from this notification.
A log file will generate an event when the firmware writes a record to the log file.
No consideration is given to the data values written to the file, if they happen to match the previous contents, the event is still generated when the file is closed.
No consideration is given to the number of data bytes written to the file, if there are none, the event is still generated when the file is closed.
This event is broadcast to all subscribed clients.

Revision.name: AfsFileChangedV1
Revision.Description: File changed (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsGetAttributes
MessageExchange.Description: Get the attributes of a file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns a file's attributes.
The locator is not intended to be interpreted by software.
Flag definitions are common to all files and file types.
No permissions are currently defined.
If the Preservable flag is false then the file should never be preserved across a DFU. If the flag is true, it doesn't necessarily mean the file should be preserved, there may be other conditions that must be met before it is safe to preserve the file. For example, context data files will be marked as true, however it is only safe to preserve them if the LPI definition of the context exactly matches in the source and target firmware.

Revision.name: AfsGetAttributesV1
Revision.Description: Get the attributes of a file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsGetCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the AFS capabilities supported by the firmware
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This returns the AFS command capabilities. Each bit in the byte array determines whether a particular capability is supported. Each command in the service has a capability command attribute that defines which of these capability bits it uses.

Revision.name: AfsGetCapabilitiesV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the AFS capabilities supported by the firmware (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsGetDirectory
MessageExchange.Description: Get a list of files present on the hearing aid
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns the number of entries in the file system's directory followed by the directory entries.
The number of entries and the entries themselves don't include hidden files, like back-up files for fail-safe files.

Revision.name: AfsGetDirectoryV1
Revision.Description: Get a list of files present on the hearing aid (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsGetFileAttributes
MessageExchange.Description: Get the attributes of the open file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns the attributes of the file currently opended by AfsOpenFile. The file can be opened in any mode.
The locator is not intended to be interpreted by software.
Flag definitions are common to all files and file types.
No permissions are currently defined.
If the Preservable flag is false then the file should never be preserved across a DFU. If the flag is true, it doesn't necessarily mean the file should be preserved, there may be other conditions that must be met before it is safe to preserve the file. For example, context data files will be marked as true, however it is only safe to preserve them if the LPI definition of the context exactly matches in the source and target firmware.
This command is deprecated in favor of the atomic file access commands AfsGetAttributes.

Revision.name: AfsGetFileAttributesV1
Revision.Description: Get the attributes of the open file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsGetVersion
MessageExchange.Description: Get the version number of the file system
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This returns the version number of the application file system. This can be used to determine the definition of the various structures such as the directory format and file attribute data structures that exist in NVM. Note that the format of the responses from AFS commands, such as AfsGetAttributes, are defined by the Piccolo protocol version and this file system version does not need to be referred to. It also carries no information about the files present, the files' formats or the files' contents.

Revision.name: AfsGetVersionV1
Revision.Description: Get the version number of the file system (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsOpenFile
MessageExchange.Description: Open a file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command opens a file. Only one file at a time can be opened. To CRC check a file it must be opened in read mode.
The Filespec is a 24 bit identifier of the file to open, it consists of a 16-bit file ID followed by an 8-bit file type ID.
Attempting to open a file that does not exist or with invalid permissions, or attempting to open another file when one is already open will cause an exception.
This command is deprecated in favor of the atomic file access commands (AfsGetAttributes, AfsRead, AfsWrite and AfsCheck).

Revision.name: AfsOpenFileV1
Revision.Description: Open a file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsRead
MessageExchange.Description: Read from a file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns data from the specified file starting at the specified offset.
If the specified length to read is zero, the command reads to the end of the file contents. For some files, the file contents might be shorter than the file length reported by the AfsGetAttributes command.
If the specified length to read plus the specified offset goes beyond the end of the file, the response is truncated at the end of the file.

Revision.name: AfsReadV1
Revision.Description: Read from a file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadBatteryUsageLog
MessageExchange.Description: Read records from the battery usage log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command reads available records from the battery usage log file which records periodic power consumption statistics so that software can profile battery usage over an extended time period. By default, records are returned in chronological order, oldest record first.
There are numerous response patterns defined for this command because the record format is different for different record types.
All log file flags are currently reserved. Set the Flags field to zero.

Revision.name: AfsReadBatteryUsageLogV1
Revision.Description: Read records from the battery usage log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadBleBisRecords
MessageExchange.Description: Read the records in the Bluetooth radio's broadcast isochronous stream (BIS) file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This file deviates from most other files in the AFS in that it uses little-endian format to store integers. Because Piccolo does not natively support little-endian integers, they are defined here as arrays of bytes.

Revision.name: AfsReadBleBisRecordsV1
Revision.Description: Read the records in the Bluetooth radio's broadcast isochronous stream (BIS) file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadBleBondKeys
MessageExchange.Description: Read the records in the Bluetooth radio's bond keys file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This file deviates from most other files in the AFS in that it uses little-endian format to store integers. Because Piccolo does not natively support little-endian integers, they are defined here as arrays of bytes.

Revision.name: AfsReadBleBondKeysV1
Revision.Description: Read the records in the Bluetooth radio's bond keys file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadBleFaultLog
MessageExchange.Description: Read the Bluetooth radio's fault log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command reads the BLE fault log file written by the Bluetooth radio at the time of a fault.
Note that despite the name, the BLE fault log is not an AFS log file, it is an ordinary file.
If the requested length is zero, the number of bytes returned may vary depending on the contents of the file.

Revision.name: AfsReadBleFaultLogV1
Revision.Description: Read the Bluetooth radio's fault log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadDfuPackage
MessageExchange.Description: Read the DFU package file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command reads the DFU package file written during the DFU download phase.
This command is intended to establish what parcels were downloaded in a previously interrupted DFU download so that it can be resumed at the appropriate point. The file contains every control parcel that was successfully sent to the aid in the previously interrupted DFU. Software should read the control parcels until it reaches the last one identified by the current control parcel count reported by DfuGetPackageInfo.
Do not assume the file is terminated (or padded) with zeros (there could be stale control parcels from a previously failed DFU).

Revision.name: AfsReadDfuPackageV1
Revision.Description: Read the DFU package file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadDirectory
MessageExchange.Description: Read the directory listing file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This command reads the directory listing file. It is similar to AfsGetDirectory but also supports reading the directory of the inactive partition.

Revision.name: AfsReadDirectoryV1
Revision.Description: Read the directory listing file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadExceptionLog
MessageExchange.Description: Read exception records from the exception log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command reads available records from the exception log file which records information about recent exceptions. By default, records are returned in chronological order, oldest record first.
There are numerous response patterns defined for this command because the exception format is different for different exception codes.
All log file flags are currently reserved. Set the Flags field to zero.

Revision.name: AfsReadExceptionLogV1
Revision.Description: Read exception records from the exception log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadExceptionTrace
MessageExchange.Description: Read exception trace file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command reads the trace file written at system init time if the system was rebooted due to an exception.
If the requested length is zero, the number of bytes returned may vary depending on the contents of the file.

Revision.name: AfsReadExceptionTraceV1
Revision.Description: Read exception trace file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadFile
MessageExchange.Description: Read from the open file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns data from the file currently opended by AfsOpenFile at the specified offset.
Attempting to read from a file not open in read mode will cause an exception.
This command is deprecated in favor of the atomic file access command AfsRead.

Revision.name: AfsReadFileV1
Revision.Description: Read from the open file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadImageSegmentLog
MessageExchange.Description: Read records from the image segment log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command reads available records from the image segment log file which stores the hashes for each segment in the original firmware package.
This file is generated at build time and is never written to by the firmware.
All log file flags are currently reserved. Set the Flags field to zero.

Revision.name: AfsReadImageSegmentLogV1
Revision.Description: Read records from the image segment log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadLog
MessageExchange.Description: Read records from a log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command reads record data from the specified log file.
A zero value for the number of records to read means read all available records, otherwise it means read up to that many records. If there are fewer records available, only the actual number available will be read.
The record index determines the starting record to read and the order in which records are read. A positive index means read from oldest to newest where zero means start from the oldest record, 1 means start from the next oldest and so on. A negative index means read from newest to oldest where -1 means start from the newest record, -2 means start from the next newest and so on.
In the response, the number of records read is the actual number of records that follow in the response.
The record size and record data do not include the size of the AFS's internal CRC that it appends to records.
Records are byte packed.
The purpose of allowing multiple records to be read is to ensure a coherent set of records are returned. If records are read individually, there is a risk that the source generating the records may get in between Piccolo requests and the result will either be duplicate records or dropped records. E.g. suppose there is a daily record generated and you ask for record -1 (Monday) and record -2 (Sunday) individually. But in between, a newer record is generated (Tuesday); now -1 refers to Tuesday, -2 is Monday. The result is that you will get Monday twice.
All log file flags are currently reserved. Set the Flags field to zero.

Revision.name: AfsReadLogV1
Revision.Description: Read records from a log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadNewBatteryLog
MessageExchange.Description: Read records from the new battery detection log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command reads available records from the new battery detection log file which records periodic battery voltage readings so that firmware can detect when the battery has been replaced or recharged. By default, records are returned in chronological order, oldest record first.
All log file flags are currently reserved. Set the Flags field to zero.

Revision.name: AfsReadNewBatteryLogV1
Revision.Description: Read records from the new battery detection log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsReadWirelessPerformanceLog
MessageExchange.Description: Read records from the wireless performance log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command reads available records from the wireless performance log file which records periodic wireless logs that can expose some firmware's internal parameters and help with root causing field issues. By default, records are returned in chronological order, oldest record first.
All log file flags are currently reserved. Set the Flags field to zero.
There are numerous response patterns defined for this command because the record format is different for different record types.
This file deviates from most other files in the AFS in that it uses little-endian format to store integers. Because Piccolo does not natively support little-endian integers, they are defined here as arrays of bytes.

Revision.name: AfsReadWirelessPerformanceLogV1
Revision.Description: Read records from the wireless performance log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsWrite
MessageExchange.Description: Write to a file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command writes data to the specified file starting at the specified offset.
Note that AFS does not support writing beyond the end of a file (only overwrite is supported).

Revision.name: AfsWriteV1
Revision.Description: Write to a file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsWriteFile
MessageExchange.Description: Write to the open file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command writes data to the file currently opended by AfsOpenFile at the specified offset.
Note that AFS does not support writing beyond the end of a file (only overwrite is supported).
Attempting to write to file not open in write mode will cause an exception.
This command is deprecated in favor of the atomic file access command AfsWrite.

Revision.name: AfsWriteFileV1
Revision.Description: Write to the open file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AfsWriteLog
MessageExchange.Description: Writes records to a log file
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command writes record data to the specified log file.
Records can only be written to the head of the log. The last record written will become the newest record.
The record size and record data do not include the size of the AFS's internal CRC that it appends to records. Records are byte packed.
This command is intended for test scenarios because there is no protection against collisions with internal firmware processes writing to the same log file. Therefore it is recommended to only use this command in factory mode where all internal firmware processes that write to log files are disabled.
All log file flags are currently reserved. Set the Flags field to zero.

Revision.name: AfsWriteLogV1
Revision.Description: Writes records to a log file (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudControlsChanged
MessageExchange.Description: Audio subsystem subsystem's programming mode control flags changed
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: The new control flags value at the time the event occurred is included with the event. Sent to all subscribed clients except the originator of the set control flags command.

Revision.name: AudControlsChangedV1
Revision.Description: Audio subsystem subsystem's programming mode control flags changed (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudGetApplets
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the supported applet IDs
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: Each bit in returned bitmap directly corresponds to an applet ID (see AudioApplets enumeration). For example, bit 0 of byte 0 corresponds to applet ID 0, bit 1 of byte 0 corresponds to applet ID 1, and so on.

Revision.name: AudGetAppletsV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the supported applet IDs (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudGetAudioAppletCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the audio applet capabilities supported by the firmware

Revision.name: AudGetAudioAppletCapabilitiesV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the audio applet capabilities supported by the firmware (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudGetCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the audio subsystem's capabilities supported by the firmware
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This returns the programming service audio subsystem command capabilities. Each bit in the byte array determines whether a particular capability is supported. Each command in the service has a capability command attribute that defines which of these capability bits it uses.

Revision.name: AudGetCapabilitiesV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the audio subsystem's capabilities supported by the firmware (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudGetControlFlags
MessageExchange.Description: Get the audio subsystem's programming mode control flags

Revision.name: AudGetControlFlagsV1
Revision.Description: Get the audio subsystem's programming mode control flags (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudGetStatus
MessageExchange.Description: Get the audio subsystem's status

Revision.name: AudGetStatusV1
Revision.Description: Get the audio subsystem's status (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudNoOp
MessageExchange.Description: No operation command

Revision.name: AudNoOpV1
Revision.Description: No operation command (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudSetControlFlags
MessageExchange.Description: Set the audio subsystem's programming mode control flags
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command sets or clears various audio subsystem control flags. Any controls that are changed are automatically restored to their original settings on exit from programming mode. Changes can only be made in programming mode.
Multiple flags can be set or multiple flags can be cleared in a single command (it is not possible to set and clear flags in a single command).
The length field can be set to any legal value. If it is shorter than the actual number of control flags bytes then only the flags corresponding to the sent mask bytes are affected. If it is longer than the actual number of control flags bytes then any excess mask bytes are ignored.

Revision.name: AudSetControlFlagsV1
Revision.Description: Set the audio subsystem's programming mode control flags (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudSoundLevelMeterStream
MessageExchange.Description: Audio sound level meter isochronous data stream
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This stream sends whole frames of sound level meter data in response to AudStartStream for stream ID StreamIdSoundLevelMeter. The number of frames can be derived from the length field.

Revision.name: AudSoundLevelMeterStreamV1
Revision.Description: Audio sound level meter isochronous data stream (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStartAdcCalibration
MessageExchange.Description: Start ADC calibration
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: It is expected that ADC calibration should only be performed in factory mode

Revision.name: AudStartAdcCalibrationV1
Revision.Description: Start ADC calibration (version 1)

Revision.name: AudStartAdcCalibrationV2
Revision.Description: Start ADC calibration (version 2)

Revision.name: AudStartAdcCalibrationV3
Revision.Description: Start ADC calibration (version 3)
Revision.EngineeringNote: Version 3 is provided to allow NumCalsToAverage to be four separate fields instead of a single array

MessageExchange.name: AudStartApplet
MessageExchange.Description: Start an audio applet
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Starts running the audio applet specified by Applet ID. Immediately sets the Applet Running bit. Applets are subprograms that can be executed on demand. There is no facility to download subprograms.
Audio applets may disrupt the normal operation of the device. Each applet must define its behavior and side effects on normal operation. It should endeavor to minimize undesirable audible artifacts.
In general, applets will automatically return to normal operation and clear the Applet Running bit. If an applet is already running, the command is ignored.

Revision.name: AudStartAppletV1
Revision.Description: Start an audio applet (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStartIndicator
MessageExchange.Description: Start an indicator
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Starts the presentation of the demo indicator. If the count is zero, the indicator is played continuously until stopped by AudStopIndicator.
The demo indicator is defined by parameters programmed into the demo indicator context. This must be programmed through the LPI interface.
If a tone or indicator is currently being played, the command is ignored.

Revision.name: AudStartIndicatorV1
Revision.Description: Start an indicator (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStartRealTimeData
MessageExchange.Description: Start real time data collection
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Starts collecting real time data as specified by the data ID. The collected data can either be read through normal LPI GET commands or via the real time service (RTS).
The ID is currently reserved and must be set to zero. The data defaults to the InputSignalAnalysis group for the RTD (Real Time Display) feature.
It is not permitted to issue another start command before stopping.
Exit from programming mode (explicitly or due to timeout) will cancel this command and stop RTD.

Revision.name: AudStartRealTimeDataV1
Revision.Description: Start real time data collection (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStartStream
MessageExchange.Description: Start streaming audio subsystem data over the isochronous streaming service
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This commands starts streaming audio subsystem data over the Piccolo isochronous streaming service (ISS) until the stream is stopped or it times out. To prevent it from timing out, keep reissuing the command within an interval of 5 minutes or less.

Revision.name: AudStartStreamV1
Revision.Description: Start streaming audio subsystem data over the isochronous streaming service (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStartTone
MessageExchange.Description: Start playing a tone
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Starts the presentation of the tone as specified in the command payload.
If a tone or indicator is currently being played, the command is ignored.
Level is specified in units of -dBFS, so a value of 6 means a level of 6 dB below full scale.

Revision.name: AudStartToneV1
Revision.Description: Start playing a tone (version 1)

Revision.name: AudStartToneV1a
Revision.Description: Start playing a tone (version 1a)
Revision.EngineeringNote: Version 1a adds tone on and off durations to version 1

MessageExchange.name: AudStatusChanged
MessageExchange.Description: Audio subsystem's status changed
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: The new status value at the time the event occurred is included with the event. This event is broadcast to all subscribed clients.

Revision.name: AudStatusChangedV1
Revision.Description: Audio subsystem's status changed (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStopApplet
MessageExchange.Description: Stop the audio applet
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Stops the applet started by AudStartApplet. Not all applets can be stopped. It is up to the applet developer to implement polling of the stop request.
The response is sent on successfully stopping the applet. If no applet is currently running, the command is ignored.

Revision.name: AudStopAppletV1
Revision.Description: Stop the audio applet (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStopIndicator
MessageExchange.Description: Stop the indicator
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: Stops the presentation of the tone started by AudStopIndicator. If no indicator is currently being played, the command is ignored.

Revision.name: AudStopIndicatorV1
Revision.Description: Stop the indicator (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStopRealTimeData
MessageExchange.Description: Stop real time data collection
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Stops the real time data collection started by AudStartRealTimeData.
The response is sent on successfully stopping the collection. Note that there might still be queued data packets to receive over the real time service (RTS) even after the collection has stopped.
If no collection is running, the command is ignored.

Revision.name: AudStopRealTimeDataV1
Revision.Description: Stop real time data collection (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStopStream
MessageExchange.Description: Stop streaming audio subsystem data over the isochronous streaming service
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This commands stops a stream that was previously started with AudStartStream. It only stops the specified stream. If the stream is already stopped, the return code will be Success.

Revision.name: AudStopStreamV1
Revision.Description: Stop streaming audio subsystem data over the isochronous streaming service (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: AudStopTone
MessageExchange.Description: Stop playing tone
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: Stops the presentation of the tone started by AudStartTone. If no tone is currently being played, the command is ignored.

Revision.name: AudStopToneV1
Revision.Description: Stop playing tone (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DebugControlsChanged
MessageExchange.Description: Debug subsystem's controls changed
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: The new control flags value at the time the event occurred is included with the event. Sent to all subscribed clients except the originator of the set control flags command.

Revision.name: DebugControlsChangedV1
Revision.Description: Debug subsystem controls changed (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DebugFilterQSpyObject
MessageExchange.Description: Filter a QSpy object
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Setting a filter removes all QSPY records for the specified object type from the debug trace output except those associated with the specified object ID. Setting the object ID to "All" clears the previous filter and allows all records for specified object type.
Each object type has its own independent filter.
Note that the firmware has to be built with the QSPY option for this command to have any effect (published packages are not built with QSPY).
The firmware may have default filters applied at compile time. This command will override those default filters.
Records will only be allowed through if they are also enabled by the DebugFilterQSpyRecord command (or by default).

Revision.name: DebugFilterQSpyObjectV1
Revision.Description: Filter a QSpy object (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DebugFilterQSpyRecord
MessageExchange.Description: Filter a QSpy record
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Enabling a filter allows QSPY records with the specified record ID to be output to the debug trace.
Typically, the firmware is has a default set of record filters enabled. This command will override those default filters.
Records will only be allowed through if they also meet the current object filter conditions.

Revision.name: DebugFilterQSpyRecordV1
Revision.Description: Filter a QSpy record (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DebugGetCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the debug subsystem's capabilities supported by the firmware
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This returns the programming service debug subsystem command capabilities. Each bit in the byte array determines whether a particular capability is supported. Each command in the service has a capability command attribute that defines which of these capability bits it uses.

Revision.name: DebugGetCapabilitiesV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the debug subsystem's capabilities supported by the firmware (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DebugGetControlFlags
MessageExchange.Description: Get the debug subsystem's programming mode control flags

Revision.name: DebugGetControlFlagsV1
Revision.Description: Get the debug subsystem's programming mode control flags (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DebugGetEnumInfo
MessageExchange.Description: Get information about an enumeration

Revision.name: DebugGetEnumInfoV1
Revision.Description: Get information about an enumeration (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DebugGetGroupInfo
MessageExchange.Description: Get information about a parameter

Revision.name: DebugGetGroupInfoV1
Revision.Description: Get information about a group (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DebugGetParameterInfo
MessageExchange.Description: Get information about a parameter

Revision.name: DebugGetParameterInfoV1
Revision.Description: Get information about a parameter (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DebugGetQSpyObjectIdCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the QSPY object ID capabilities supported by the firmware

MessageExchange.name: DevGetEnumCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the capabilities supported by an enumeration definition of this firmware
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This returns the capabilities of an enumeration definition. Each bit in the byte array determines whether a particular item is supported in the definition.
Refer to PiccoloProtocol.xml to determine the association between byte and bit position in the response and the item definition.
If the length returned is zero then either the enumeration ID doesn't exist or it doesn't support capabilities.
Note that a supported item doesn't necessarily mean it is present in a specific enumeration of the enumeration definition. Refer to the appropriate PiccoloProtocol.xml to determine whether an item is in a specific enumeration. However, use of this capabilities command to determine supported items is orthogonal to the use of multiple enumerations in PiccoloProtocol.xml. Commands that support an arbitrary set of items (such as UiExecFeature) will use this mechanism whereas commands that support specific sets of items per command revision will use the multiple enumerations mechanism and will not have a response to this command.
The presence of a enumeration item capability bit does not necessarily mean that the corresponding functionality is supported. It only means that the command that uses the enumeration will understand it as a known item. There can be many reasons why the function itself might not operate (for example; hardware configuration, current mode of the aid, business logic enforced by parameters, obsolete features, etc.)

Revision.name: DevGetEnumCapabilitiesV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the capabilities supported by an enumeration definition of this firmware (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DevRequestProgrammingMode
MessageExchange.Description: Request entry into or exit from programming mode
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Requests entry to or exit from programming mode. Returns response to indicate whether request is granted. Entry or exit will be denied if another client is in programming mode (the response will be AlreadyInUse). Only the interface that entered programming mode can exit programming mode.
ForceReinit and ForceExit flags are only applicable for the Wireless interface. Firmware ignores them if a wired client enters programming mode.
On wireless disconnection or inactivity timeout, firmware exits programming mode immediately and resets all services on the wireless interface. The wireless timeout in use by the firmware can be read via the SysGetProgrammingModeTimeout command. See SupResetServices for the actions performed when all services are reset.
For the purposes of determining wireless activity for the ForceExit flag, only the following is considered to be activity. The traffic must come from the same wireless client that requested programming mode. Only Piccolo traffic is considered. Only incoming requests are considered (outgoing responses on any service do not count).
Exiting programming mode automatically re-enables any disabled subsystems and returns all control flags to their default states (inhibit flags off and force flags off).
It is not recommended to chain any additional commands after this command in the same transport packet because it might not be successful at entering programming mode and therefore any following commands that assume programming mode might cause a firmware exception.
The "not ready" response will never be returned in normal operation (it is a corner case that might occur in a development environment). In future, the response might return other non-zero error codes so do not rely on any value other than zero.
If a client has already been granted programming mode and it makes another request to enter programming mode, it will be granted. The flags in the second request take precedence over the original request. For example, if ForceExit flag had been set on the first request but not the second, then it will no longer be in ForceExit mode and the inactivity timer will be cancelled. Firmware does not support programming mode nesting. For example, if two requests are made to enter programming mode, the next request to exit programming mode will immediately exit programming mode.
Firmware with only revision DevRequestProgrammingModeV1 causes a firmware exception if programming mode is reentered (nested) with the ForceExit flag set on both the outer and inner requests. Check the capability bit for revision DevRequestProgrammingModeV1a to determine if this is fixed in the firmware.

Revision.name: DevRequestProgrammingModeV1
Revision.Description: Request entry into or exit from programming mode (version 1)

Revision.name: DevRequestProgrammingModeV1a
Revision.Description: Request entry into or exit from programming mode (version 1a)
Revision.EngineeringNote: Version 1a is provided to determine if the ForceExit flag is usable. See the notes for this command.

MessageExchange.name: DevServiceException
MessageExchange.Description: Service exception occurred
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This event is generated when a service exception occurs and the client making the service request is subscribed to this event. It is only sent to the offending client.
If this event is not subscribed to by the client that originated the request that caused the exception, then the hearing aid uses its regular exception handling mechanism (reboot).
The service that caused the exception will have been reset and any pending commands and responses aborted.
If the request packet that contained the command that caused the exception had other commands preceding the offending command, those commands might have succeeded although any pending successful responses will be lost.
If the request packet that contained the command that caused the exception had other commands following the offending command, those commands will be abandoned.
If the request packet that contained the command that caused the exception required additional request packets to complete, software should abandon those additional request packets.
If this occurs, it is advisable for software to issue a SupResetServices command to get the interface back to a known state.
Exception codes match the QP exception codes used in DevGetException.

Revision.name: DevServiceExceptionV1
Revision.Description: Service exception occurred (version 1)

MessageExchange.Description: Service exception for QP error occurred
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: See DevServiceException for details

MessageExchange.name: DfuGetPackageCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the DFU package capabilities supported by the firmware
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns a bitmap as follows:
Byte 0, Bit 0 - Firmware supports package version 1.0 (deprecated package format with combined NVM and script parcels) Byte 0, Bit 1 - Firmware supports package version 2.0 (current package format) Byte 0, Bit 2 - Firmware supports package version 2.1 (format 2.0 plus implicit integrity check in NVM data) Byte 0, Bit 3 - Firmware supports package version 2.2 (format 2.1 plus support for compressed blocks) Byte 0, Bit 4 - Firmware supports package version 2.3 (format 2.2 plus support for incremental DFU using BeginNvmBlockCopy/EndNvmBlockCopy) Byte 0, Bit 5 - Firmware supports package version 2.4 (format 2.3 plus support for bookmarks) Byte 0, Bit 6 - Firmware supports package version 2.5 (format 2.4 plus support for file download) Byte 0, Bit 7 - Firmware supports package version 2.6 (format 2.5 plus support for differential NVM blocks)
For each bit in the bitmap:
0 = Capability is not supported 1 = Capability is supported

MessageExchange.name: DfuSetControlFlags
MessageExchange.Description: Set the DFU subsystem's programming mode control flags
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command sets or clears various DFU subsystem control flags. Any controls that are changed are automatically restored to their original settings on exit from programming mode. Changes can only be made in programming mode.
Multiple flags can be set or multiple flags can be cleared in a single command (it is not possible to set and clear flags in a single command).
The length field can be set to any legal value. If it is shorter than the actual number of control flags bytes then only the flags corresponding to the sent mask bytes are affected. If it is longer than the actual number of control flags bytes then any excess mask bytes are ignored.

Revision.Description: Set the DFU subsystem's programming mode control flags (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DfuStatusChanged
MessageExchange.Description: DFU subsystem's status changed
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
The new status value at the time the event occurred is included with the event. This event is broadcast to all subscribed clients.
Not all changes to the error field generate ENS events. When firmware clears the error field at the start of a command, no event is generated. If a DfuWriteParcel command fails due to an error, no event is generated (the error code is returned immediately in the command's response).

Revision.name: DfuStatusChangedV1
Revision.Description: DFU subsystem's status changed (version 1)

Revision.name: DfuStatusChangedV1a
Revision.Description: DFU subsystem's status changed (version 1a)

MessageExchange.name: DfuWriteParcel
MessageExchange.Description: Write a DFU parcel
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
All parcels written as part of a single DFU must have matching DFU ID.
The format shown here is for a 16-byte parcel which covers all control parcels but only the smallest data parcel size. For larger parcel sizes, the ParcelData field size is according to the ParcelSize field (which uses the DfuParcelSizes enumeration) and the Crc field always immediately follows the ParcelData.
See AfsReadDfuPackage command for a description of the control parcel formats.

Revision.name: DfuWriteParcelV1
Revision.Description: Write a DFU parcel (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: DfuWriteParcelAsync
MessageExchange.Description: Write a DFU parcel asynchronously
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is similar to AfsWriteParcel except that it responds immediately with an initial return code. Provided the return code is "None", the parcel write then proceeds in the background. While the parcel write proceeds in the background, the ParcelWriteInProgress DFU status bit is set. If the return code is anything other than "None", the write does not proceed and the status bit does not get set.
If another DfuWriteParcel or DfuWriteParcelAsync is attempted while an asynchronous write is in progress, the return code will be "NotReadyForParcel". The same parcel can then be retried until the return code is "None".
It is not recommended to split a DfuWriteParcelAsync parcel across multiple transport packets because the aid cannot start asynchronous processing until the entire parcel has been received and it cannot receive a second packet until the first packet has been fully synchronously processed.
This command minimizes the latency imposed on other Piccolo programming service commands and is especially useful when the parcel may cause a lot of data to be written to NVM. One case is when a compressed parcel expands to a much larger size (such as a large run of zeros). Another case is an EndNvmBlockCopy control parcel that can trigger a large block copy.

Revision.name: DfuWriteParcelAsyncV1
Revision.Description: Write a DFU parcel asynchronously (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiCheckParameters
MessageExchange.Description: Generate a CRC checksum of LPI parameter values
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
The bitstream format is defined on the Lamarr LPI VLC Commands page. This command checks the parameters specified in the request bitstream. The response contains the CRC of the parameter values.
The CRC is calculated across all parameter values in the order given. The data bytes are considered to be formatted identically to that described for the LpiSet/GetParameters commands.
This is the CRC according to the CRC16-CCITT standard using the polynomial 0x1021 and an initial seed of 0xFFFF. The most significant byte is returned first.

Revision.name: LpiCheckParametersV1
Revision.Description: Generate a CRC checksum of LPI parameter values (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiContextChanged
MessageExchange.Description: LPI context changed
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
It is not guaranteed that the context data will have changed (the original data overwritten by the LPI set command is not compared).
Many parameters in many groups may change in a context due to a single LPI set command, only one notification will be generated in such cases.
Only changes to parameters in cacheable groups cause notification. Changes to parameters in non-cacheable groups are ignored for purposes of this event.
This event is not sent to the originator of the LPI set command. The purpose of this event is for software applications to be able to invalidate their parameter cache when another application changes one of their cached parameters.
Cacheable parameters are never written autonomously by the firmware, therefore this event is only ever generated in response to an LPI set command. This notification only indicates that the logical context changed, it is not related to the corresponding physical parameters changing which may require a context refresh to occur.
LpiCopyGroupsById will also generate this event if any of the destination groups are cacheable.

Revision.name: LpiContextChangedV1
Revision.Description: LPI context changed (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiCopyGroupsById
MessageExchange.Description: Copy groups from one context to another context
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
The specified groups must exist in both the source and target contexts. Both contexts must be AFS contexts. If the target context is auto-refresh, it will not be automatically refreshed. If any target group is cacheable, this command will clear the cookies of other clients. If the count is zero, it will copy all groups that are common to both the source and target contexts.
If non-existent IDs are supplied, the command may return GroupNotFound or ContextNotFound. If the list of groups contains good and bad IDs, then GroupNotFound is returned and the set of successfully copied groups is undefined.

Revision.name: LpiCopyGroupsByIdV1
Revision.Description: Copy groups from one context to another context (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiGetCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the logical parameter interface (LPI) capabilities supported by the firmware
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This returns the programming service LPI command capabilities. Each bit in the byte array determines whether a particular capability is supported. Each command in the service has a capability command attribute that defines which of these capability bits it uses.

Revision.name: LpiGetCapabilitiesV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the logical parameter interface (LPI) capabilities supported by the firmware (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiGetCompressedParameters
MessageExchange.Description: Get LPI compressed parameter values
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command gets the parameters specified in the request bitstream. The response bitstream contains the parameter values. Multi-element parameter data values are compressed using a form of delta-coding.
The bitstream format is defined on the Lamarr LPI VLC Commands page.

Revision.name: LpiGetCompressedParametersV1
Revision.Description: Get LPI compressed parameter values (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiGetContext
MessageExchange.Description: Get all the LPI parameters in a context
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command gets all of the parameters in all of the groups in a context.
The parameter values are all of arbitrary bit width and are all bit packed together within groups. Each group is byte aligned by zero-padding the last byte of the group.
In order to parse the parameter values data bytes received, the caller has to be aware of the parameter bit widths, parameter order in the parameter group, and group order in the context.
Version 2 provides support for context indices greater than 255.

Revision.name: LpiGetContextV1
Revision.Description: Get all the LPI parameters in a context (version 1)

Revision.name: LpiGetContextV2
Revision.Description: Get all the LPI parameters in a context (version 2)

MessageExchange.name: LpiGetCookie
MessageExchange.Description: Get the LPI cookie value
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command gets the cookie belonging to the calling client. The wired connection and all the various wireless connection Piccolo GATT characteristics are considered separate clients.
If no cookie has been ever been set for the calling client, the returned value is zero. If any other client has written to a cacheable parameter since the cookie was set, the returned value is zero.

Revision.name: LpiGetCookieV1
Revision.Description: Get the LPI cookie value (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiGetDiscoveryInfo
MessageExchange.Description: Get the LPI discovery information
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: The discovery data format is available on the Lamarr LPI Discovery wiki page.

Revision.name: LpiGetDiscoveryInfoV1
Revision.Description: Get the LPI discovery information (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiGetParameterArrayById
MessageExchange.Description: Get a single LPI parameter's array element values by ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
If the datatype of the parameter is an enumerated type, then the bits per element is always 16, otherwise it is the element size of the LPI parameter on the device.
The number of elements that can be requested is limited only by the number of elements in the parameter. If the return data does not fit in a single packet, it will be returned in multiple packets ("extended packetization").
If an error occurs, the bits per element is returned as zero and effectively no data is returned.

Revision.name: LpiGetParameterArrayByIdV1
Revision.Description: Get a single LPI parameter's array element values by ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiGetParameterById
MessageExchange.Description: Get a single LPI parameter value by ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
If the parameter has multiple elements, then only the first element will be returned. To access other elements, use LpiGetParameterArrayById.
If the datatype of the parameter is an enumerated type, then the data returned is the ID of the enumerated item value (16-bit ID zero-extended to 32-bit).
If the datatype of the parameter is fixed point, then the normalized return data can be converted to floating point by multiplying by 2^n. Note that n can be different to the caller's knowledge of the parameter's fractional bits.
If an error occurs, then undefined 32-bit data is returned.
Suppose the bytes returned are F2 FF FF FF E6, that means the returned value is signed, float_conversion is -4, and the normalized value is 0xFFFFFFE6 = -26. To convert back to a float, multiply by 2^n (where n is -4). So, -26 * (2^-4) = -1.625.

Revision.name: LpiGetParameterByIdV1
Revision.Description: Get a single LPI parameter value by ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiGetParameters
MessageExchange.Description: Get LPI parameter values
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command gets the parameters specified in the request bitstream. The response bitstream contains the parameter values.
The bitstream format is defined on the Lamarr LPI VLC Commands page.

Revision.name: LpiGetParametersV1
Revision.Description: Get LPI parameter values (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiGetVersion
MessageExchange.Description: Get the version number of the logical parameter interface (LPI) definition

Revision.name: LpiGetVersionV1
Revision.Description: Get the version number of the logical parameter interface (LPI) definition (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiRefreshContextById
MessageExchange.Description: Refresh an LPI context by ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Note that unless the return code error is "success", the refresh does not take effect.
Contexts of type "reinit" are not refreshed.

Revision.name: LpiRefreshContextByIdV1
Revision.Description: Refresh an LPI context by ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiRefreshContexts
MessageExchange.Description: Refresh all of the parameters in one or more LPI contexts
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command refreshes all of the parameters in all of the groups in one or more contexts.
A context count of zero means refresh all contexts.
Refreshing a context notifies the firmware that a context has been changed. Firmware will take whatever action is necessary to reapply the entire context so that the changes can take effect. Contexts can be provided in any order; they are refreshed in the order specified.
In order to reapply a context, firmware may have to reinitialize some internal functions and this may cause side effects (such as stopping and restarting audio).
Refresh does not cause control actions. For example, refreshing memory context 1 when memory 2 is the current memory does not cause the device to switch to memory 1.
Refresh does not necessarily have any effect on the current parameters in use. For example, refreshing memory context 1 when memory 2 is the current memory will have no effect.
Not all contexts have refresh support. This will be indicated in the LPI definition. Some contexts can only be refreshed with a device reset or device reinit. Refreshing such contexts has no effect.
Refresh has no effect on "auto-refresh" contexts, since, by definition, auto-refresh contexts are self-refreshing.

Revision.name: LpiRefreshContextsV1
Revision.Description: Refresh all of the parameters in one or more LPI contexts (version 1)

Revision.name: LpiRefreshContextsV2
Revision.Description: Refresh all of the parameters in one or more LPI contexts (version 2)

MessageExchange.name: LpiResetParameters
MessageExchange.Description: Reset all parameters in non-cacheable output groups in AFS file contexts to their default values
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is intended for setting parameters to their default values.
Here, default values means their values as defined by this command. These values are not necessarily the same as the firmware defaults listed in the CSV files distributed with firmware packages. And they are not necessarily the same as the values reported by Xano.
In general, defaults are set to zero as follows:
Integers, bytes and fixed point values are set to zero Enumerated types are set to the item with the index value of zero Boolean values are set to FALSE UTF-8 types are set to an empty string (all zeros) DateTime types are set to a null date (all zeros)
The following exceptions apply (if not in factory mode):
BatteryCapacity is set to the value of StandardBatteryCapacity FbcBulkDelayEstimate is set to 1.1 ms BootCount, BleRadioBootCount and BleRadioFirmwareTransferCount are not reset
This command has no effect on LPI cookies because cookies only apply to cacheable parameters and, by definition, this command only applies to non-cacheable parameters.
Since output parameters are under the control of firmware, there is no guarantee that any parameters reset by this command will remain at their reset values for any particular length of time.
In factory mode, this command resets all the non-cacheable output groups in AFS file contexts to zero but does not apply any of the exceptions listed above. Since writing to such parameters is permitted in factory mode, software can then set whatever defaults it wants.
Due to a bug, revision 1.0 (V1) of this command is broken, use capability bit for revision 1.1 (V1a) to check support for the fixed command.

Revision.name: LpiResetParametersV1
Revision.Description: Reset all parameters in non-cacheable output groups in AFS file contexts to their default values (version 1)

Revision.name: LpiResetParametersV1a
Revision.Description: Reset all parameters in non-cacheable output groups in AFS file contexts to their default values (version 1a)

MessageExchange.name: LpiRestoreParameterArrayById
MessageExchange.Description: Restore a single LPI parameter's array element values by ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Note that unless the return code is "success", not all values may be written.
If the element count is zero, all elements must be supplied. The data format of the parameter values must exactly match the response from LpiGetParameterArrayById.
Unlike LpiSetParameterArrayById, the element size is always the element size of the LPI parameter on the device. Parameters of enumerated type take the item index, not the item ID.
Intended to be used internally by DFU to restore parameter values.

Revision.name: LpiRestoreParameterArrayByIdV1
Revision.Description: Restore a single LPI parameter's array element values by ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiSaveParameterArrayById
MessageExchange.Description: Save a single LPI parameter's array element values by ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Unlike LpiGetParameterArrayById, the element size is always the element size of the LPI parameter on the device. Parameters of enumerated type return the item index, not the item ID.
Intended to be used internally by DFU to save parameter values

Revision.name: LpiSaveParameterArrayByIdV1
Revision.Description: Save a single LPI parameter's array element values by ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiSetCompressedParameters
MessageExchange.Description: Set LPI compressed parameter values
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command sets the parameters specified in the bitstream. The bitstream includes inline parameter values. Multi-element parameter data values are compressed using a form of delta-coding.
Parameter values in groups that are defined as output-only are unaffected by this command (unless the parameter is in an AFS context and the aid is in factory mode).
The bitstream format is defined on the Lamarr LPI VLC Commands page.
Due to a bug, revision 1.0 (V1) of this command does not support extended packetization, use the capability bit for revision 1.1 (V1a) to check for the fixed version.

Revision.name: LpiSetCompressedParametersV1
Revision.Description: Set LPI compressed parameter values (version 1)

Revision.name: LpiSetCompressedParametersV1a
Revision.Description: Set LPI compressed parameter values (version 1a)

MessageExchange.name: LpiSetContext
MessageExchange.Description: Set all the LPI parameters in a context
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command sets all of the parameters in all of the groups in a context.
The parameter values are all of arbitrary bit width and are all bit packed together within groups. Each group is byte aligned by zero-padding the last byte of the group.
In order to form the parameter values data bytes sent, the caller has to be aware of the parameter bit widths, parameter order in the parameter group, and group order in the context. Parameters of array type must be fully specified (the value of all entries in the array).
Parameter values in groups that are defined as output-only are unaffected by this command (unless the context is an AFS context and the aid is in factory mode).
Version 2 provides support for context indices greater than 255.

Revision.name: LpiSetContextV1
Revision.Description: Set all the LPI parameters in a context (version 1)

Revision.name: LpiSetContextV2
Revision.Description: Set all the LPI parameters in a context (version 2)

MessageExchange.name: LpiSetCookie
MessageExchange.Description: Set the LPI cookie value
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command sets a cookie for use by the client to track the state of its LPI cache. The cookie's value is held independently per client. The cookie is held persistently (i.e. maintained across power cycles). A client's cookie is cleared (set to zero) if any other client writes to a cacheable parameter.
Each Piccolo GATT characteristic (access point) on each BLE connection is considered a separate client. Therefore, if a client sets a cookie using one access point and then another client writes to a cacheable parameter using a different access point on the same BLE connection, then the cookie will be cleared. If a client sets a cookie using one access point and then another client writes to a cacheable parameter using the same access point on a different BLE connection, then the cookie will be cleared. The aid does not necessarily keep the maximum number of possible cookies (the number of access points times the number of bonded devices could be over one hundred) and so it is possible that a cookie will be lost (cleared) even if a cacheable parameter wasn't written.
The algorithm for determining the value of the cookie to set is outside the scope of this specification but it should be some unique non-zero value such as a value derived from a random number generator or a timestamp.

Revision.name: LpiSetCookieV1
Revision.Description: Set the LPI cookie value (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiSetParameterArrayById
MessageExchange.Description: Set a single LPI parameter's array element values by ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Note that unless the return code is "success", not all values may be written.
The rules for "float_conversion" and "signed" are the same as LpiSetParameterById.
If the datatype is bool, the bits per element should be 1, if UTF-8 the bits per element should be 8, if enum the bits per element should be 16. For integer and fixed point, any width (1 to 32) is permitted (regardless of the logical parameter definition).
The number of elements that can be written is limited only by the number of elements in the parameter. If the data does not fit in a single packet, it can be sent in multiple packets ("extended packetization").
If the zero pad flag is set and the last element provided in the command is not the last element in the array, then the remaining element values will be filled with zeros. This can be used for any parameter type but is intended for ensuring that a UTF-8 parameter is not left with trailing garbage characters when a shorter string is written. Note that zeros are not always legal values for some parameter types so this flag should only be used when appropriate. If the parameter is an enumerated type, the zero padding will treated as item IDs of zero and translated to the appropriate item index.

Revision.name: LpiSetParameterArrayByIdV1
Revision.Description: Set a single LPI parameter's array element values by ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiSetParameterById
MessageExchange.Description: Set a single LPI parameter value by ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Note that unless the return code error is "Success", the value is not written.
If the parameter has multiple elements, then only the first element will be written. To access other elements, use LpiSetParameterArrayById.
If the datatype of the parameter is an enumerated type, then the data written is the ID of the enumerated item value (16-bit ID zero-extended to 32-bit).
If the datatype of the parameter is fixed point, then the originating floating point value should be normalized by dividing by 2^n. Where n is the negative of the number of fractional bits of the logical parameter (to the best of the caller's knowledge). If the firmware is using fewer fractional bits than the software expects then be aware that reading the value back may result in some loss of precision (the least significant fractional bits will truncated by the firmware).
If the datatype of the parameter is not fixed point then the "float_conversion" field must be zero.
The "signed" bit may only be set if the datatype is integer or fixed point.
Suppose the value that you to wish to set is -1.625 and the parameter has 1 sign bit, 3 integer and 4 fractional bits. The float should be "normalized" by dividing by the float conversion 2^n where n is -4. Then -1.625 / (2^-4) = -26 = 0xFFFFFFE6. Therefore the bytes after the context and parameter IDs are F2 FF FF FF E6.

Revision.name: LpiSetParameterByIdV1
Revision.Description: Set a single LPI parameter value by ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: LpiSetParameters
MessageExchange.Description: Set LPI parameter values
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command sets the parameters specified in the bitstream. The bitstream includes inline parameter values.
Parameter values in groups that are defined as output-only are unaffected by this command (unless the parameter is in an AFS context and the aid is in factory mode).
The bitstream format is defined on the Lamarr LPI VLC Commands page.

Revision.name: LpiSetParametersV1
Revision.Description: Set LPI parameter values (version 1)

Multiple flags can be set or multiple flags can be cleared in a single command (it is not possible to set and clear flags in a single command).

Inhibiting NFMI operation prevents any NFMI incoming or outgoing traffic. It does not prevent access to NFMI memory targets and it does not prevent any of the NFMI sub-command from being accepted (however not all sub-commands are appropriate outside of normal operation).
Forcing power down should be used with care. Intended for specific test-purposes only. May cause undefined behavior if device attempts to use the NFMI subsystem. Other than the mandatory ones, none of the NFMI sub-commands are appropriate when forcing power down and none of the NFMI memory targets are appropriate for memory transfer device commands. Force power down cannot be issued if the NFMI subsystem is disabled (however it can be issued if NFMI operation is inhibited).
Forcing stay alive will prevent the WiCROS transmitter from powering down due to loss of activity detected from the WiCROS receiver. The inactivity timeout will be reset when the flag is cleared (explicitly or on exit from programming mode). This is intended to prevent the WiCROS transmitter powering itself down during an extended fitting session. Note that the flag must be set for at least one second for the timeout reset to occur, otherwise the inactivity timeout might be unaffected.

MessageExchange.name: RfSetControlFlags
MessageExchange.Description: Set the RF subsystem's programming mode control flags
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command sets or clears various RF subsystem control flags. Any controls that are changed are automatically restored to their original settings on exit from programming mode. Changes can only be made in programming mode.
Multiple flags can be set or multiple flags can be cleared in a single command (it is not possible to set and clear flags in a single command).
The length field can be set to any legal value. If it is shorter than the actual number of control flags bytes then only the flags corresponding to the sent mask bytes are affected. If it is longer than the actual number of control flags bytes then any excess mask bytes are ignored.
The force radio power down bit is intended for electrical test purposes only. Support for returning to normal operation is undefined (a full manual reboot will probably be required). It is TBD what other functions will be permitted when radio is powered down.
When scatternet is disabled, all wireless connections are dropped (apart from the programmer connection). This bit has no effect if wireless operation is inhibited.

MessageExchange.name: RfSetHighSpeedMode
MessageExchange.Description: Set the Bluetooth connection to high speed mode
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: Puts this wireless connection into high speed mode. Does not affect connections to other devices. High speed mode times out after 2 minutes. High speed mode is cancelled if the connection is dropped. To maintain high speed mode, send this command periodically. High speed mode attempts to set the connection interval to 10mS. If the attempt fails the next longer interval is tried in 1.25mS increments. The threshold for high speed mode status is any interval shorter than 20mS. The command is implemented for programmers and Android connections. The command is ignored for iOS connections because iOS does not support faster connection intervals.

MessageExchange.name: RfTestResultCrystalTrim
MessageExchange.Description: RF test result for RfStartCrystalTrimTest
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This event is sent when the RF subsystem completes a crystal trim test. Broadcast to all subscribed clients.
The reported trim value is in units of 0.4 pF. If it is at the limit of the range (0 or 63) then the counter offset can be used to determine whether the accuracy is sufficient. The counter offsets are measuring the 32 kHz crystal against the 48MHz crystal, therefore positive values mean the 32 kHz clock is too slow. The accuracy in ppm can be calculated using the following equation; ppm = offset / 750000 * 1000000. It is up to the user of the RfStartCrystalTrimTest command to determine whether the accuracy of the crystal after trimming is considered acceptable.

MessageExchange.name: RtsRequestData
MessageExchange.Description: Request real time data response packets
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns repeated response structures at a rate determined by the current streaming mode that the device is in.
If an empty response is immediately received (a packet with a zero-length payload and flow control clear), then no real time data (RTD) has been started.
If RTD has been started, RTS will keep returning response packets with the flow control bit set until it is stopped. When RTD is stopped, RTS will have stopped when it returns a packet with the flow control bit clear. Note that stopping RTD is a programming service command which is asynchronous to RTS, so don't assume that the response immediately after the stop RTD command will be the final RTS response, an actual response may already be in flight.
While RTS is returning response packets over an extended period, it may also return "keep-alive" packets (zero length payload with flow control set). These can be ignored.
Currently, the only supported streaming mode for RTS is RTD. See AudStartRealTimeData.
This command is only available if the client requesting it has been granted programming mode via the programming service.

Revision.name: RtsRequestDataV1
Revision.Description: Request real time data response packets (version 1)
