MessageExchange.name: ScriptSaveContext
MessageExchange.Description: Save context with specified ID (generate restore context command in target script)
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is the method for preserving a context across a DFU. It is to be executed in the source script. Generates a matching-sized ScriptRestoreFile command in the target script. An exception will occur if the target context data file does not exist or if the target context data file is smaller than the source.
It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that it is appropriate to copy the context. Contexts should only be copied if the contexts' definitions in PiccoloInterface.xml are identical. If not, then groups and/or parameters will have to be saved individually.

Revision.name: ScriptSaveContextV1
Revision.Description: Save context with specified ID (generate restore context command in target script) (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: ScriptSaveContexts
MessageExchange.Description: Save a list of contexts with specified indices (generate restore contexts command in target script)
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is a method for preserving multiple contexts across a DFU. It is to be executed in the source script and generates a ScriptRestoreContexts command in the target script. An exception will occur if the context does not exist in both the source and target. Each context must be specified by its index in the target PiccoloInterface.xml.
For the purposes of calculating the resulting target script size, this command generates a target script command of size = 2 + count bytes.
It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that it is appropriate to copy the contexts. Contexts should only be copied if the contexts' definitions in PiccoloInterface.xml are identical. If not, then groups and/or parameters will have to be saved individually.
Version 2 provides support for context indices greater than 255.

Revision.name: ScriptSaveContextsV1
Revision.Description: Save contexts with specified indices (generate restore contexts command in target script) (version 1)

Revision.name: ScriptSaveContextsV2
Revision.Description: Save contexts with specified indices (generate restore contexts command in target script) (version 2)

MessageExchange.name: ScriptSaveFile
MessageExchange.Description: Save file with specified ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is the method for preserving a file across a DFU. It is to be executed in the source script. Generates a matching-sized ScriptRestoreFile command in the target script. An exception will occur if the target file does not exist or if the target file is smaller than the source.
The Filespec is a 24 bit identifier of the file to save, it consists of a 16-bit file ID followed by an 8-bit file type ID.
It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that it is appropriate to copy the file. In general, files should only be saved if the source and target files have matching versions and the preservable property is true in the manifest.xml. Context data files should only be copied if the contexts definitions in PiccoloInterface.xml are identical.
This command can be used to save general files (such as the voice data file) and for saving contexts. See ScriptSaveContext.

Revision.name: ScriptSaveFileV1
Revision.Description: Save file with specified ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: ScriptSaveGroup
MessageExchange.Description: Save a parameter group with specified ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is the method for preserving a parameter group across a DFU. It is to be executed in the source script. Generates a corresponding ScriptRestoreGroup command in the target script.
It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that it is appropriate to save and restore the group. Groups should only be saved and restored if the group definitions in PiccoloInterface.xml are identical in the source and target (same group major and minor versions).
For the purposes of calculating the resulting target script size, this command generates a target script command of size = 9 bytes.
If the parameter group doesn't exist in the source or target an exception will occur when the script is executed.

Revision.name: ScriptSaveGroupV1
Revision.Description: Save a parameter group with specified ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: ScriptSaveGroups
MessageExchange.Description: Save a list of groups with specified IDs from a single context (generate restore groups command in target script)
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is a method for preserving multiple groups across a DFU. It is to be executed in the source script and generates a ScriptRestoreGroups command in the target script. An exception will occur if the context and groups do not exist in both the source and target.
For the purposes of calculating the resulting target script size, this command generates a target script command of size = 4 + 5 * count bytes.
It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that it is appropriate to copy the groups. Groups should only be copied if the groups definitions in PiccoloInterface.xml are identical. If not, then parameters will have to be saved individually.

Revision.name: ScriptSaveGroupsV1
Revision.Description: Save groups with specified IDs from a single context (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: ScriptSaveParameter
MessageExchange.Description: Save the value of the specified parameter
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is the method for preserving a single element parameter across a DFU. It is to be executed in the source script. Generates a corresponding ScriptStoreParameter command in the target script.
The format of this command is identical to LpiGetParameterById. If the parameter has multiple elements, only the first element will be saved.
For the purposes of calculating the resulting target script size, this command generates a target script command of size = 10 bytes.
If the parameter doesn't exist in the source or target an exception will occur when the script is executed.

Revision.name: ScriptSaveParameterV1
Revision.Description: Save the value of the specified parameter (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: ScriptSaveParameterArray
MessageExchange.Description: Save the element values of the specified parameter array
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is the method for preserving a multi-element parameter across a DFU. It is to be executed in the source script. Generates a corresponding ScriptStoreParameterArray command in the target script.
The format of this command is identical to LpiGetParameterArrayById.
For the purposes of calculating the resulting target script size, this command generates a target script command of size = 11 + floor((7+element_count*bit_width)/8) bytes.
If the parameter or specified elements don't exist in the source or target an exception will occur when the script is executed. If the specified element count is zero (which means save all elements) no exception will occur when the source and target element counts are different.

Revision.name: ScriptSaveParameterArrayV1
Revision.Description: Save the element values of the specified parameter array (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: ScriptSaveParameters
MessageExchange.Description: Save a list of parameters with specified IDs from a single context (generate restore parameters command in target script)
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is a method for preserving multiple parameters across a DFU. It is to be executed in the source script and generates a ScriptRestoreParameters command in the target script. An exception will occur if the context and parameters do not exist in both the source and target. All elements of multi-element parameters are saved.
For the purposes of calculating the resulting target script size, this command generates a target script command of size = 4 + floor((sum(size_in_bits(parameter_info[])) + 7) / 8). i.e. the size is 4 bytes plus all of the parameter_info structures tightly bit-packed (and bit-padded to byte alignment at the very end). The size of each parameter_info structure is calculated as size_in_bits = (16 + element_size_in_bits * element_count). The bit width of enumerated parameter type elements is the defined width of the item indices (not the width of the item IDs).
It is the responsibility of the user to ensure that it is appropriate to copy the parameters. Parameters should only be copied if the parameters' definitions in PiccoloInterface.xml are identical (specifically; all of the bit counts, number of elements, min/max range, enumeration and enumerated item references). It is acceptable for the parameter to have moved to a different group within the same context. If not identical, but forward compatible, then parameters can be saved individually using ScriptSaveParameter.
Due to a bug, revision 1.0 (V1) of this command is broken, use capability bit for revision 1.1 (V1a) to check support for the fixed command.

Revision.name: ScriptSaveParametersV1
Revision.Description: Save parameters with specified IDs from a single context (version 1)

Revision.name: ScriptSaveParametersV1a
Revision.Description: Save parameters with specified IDs from a single context (version 1a)

MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:

MessageExchange.Description: Update an arbitrary set of compressed parameters (generate store compressed parameters command in target script)

MessageExchange.name: SrSetControlFlags

MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command sets or clears various smart reminders subsystem control flags. Any controls that are changed are automatically restored to their original settings on exit from programming mode. Changes can only be made in programming mode.
Multiple flags can be set or multiple flags can be cleared in a single command (it is not possible to set and clear flags in a single command).
The length field can be set to any legal value. If it is shorter than the actual number of control flags bytes then only the flags corresponding to the sent mask bytes are affected. If it is longer than the actual number of control flags bytes then any excess mask bytes are ignored.

MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the supervisor service capabilities supported by the firmware
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This returns the supervisor service command capabilities. Each bit in the byte array determines whether a particular capability is supported. Each command in the service has a capability command attribute that defines which of these capability bits it uses.

MessageExchange.name: SupGetInterfaceStatus
MessageExchange.Description: Get the status of one of the Piccolo interfaces
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Piccolo has a number of communication interface instances. The first one is always the wired interface and the remaining are dynamically assigned as necessary to wireless interfaces.
The busy flag will always be true for an interface if it is queried by a client on the same interface (because it is busy processing this command). The busy flag is not currently implemented for the wired interface.
A DeviceId of None means the interface is not allocated to a client.
The reference count is an internal count of how many times the interface is being referenced by its current client. Examples of things that cause the reference count to be incremented are; incoming requests, outgoing events, incomplete requests (due to fragmentation or multi-packet requests), and acquiring programming mode. An interface is not released until the reference count returns to zero. If the ManagedSingleClientEnable parameter is true, the reference count will not drop below one until the BLE connection is terminated. The reference count is not valid for the wired interface.
The active index is an internal index of the Piccolo client that is actively communicating over an interface. There is a limit of 3 simultaneous BLE connections and a limit of 7 access points per BLE connection and therefore a maximum of 21 active wireless clients. Index 0 is for the wired interface. The remaining indices are 1 through 21 and are calculated as 1 + 7*(BLE connection index) + (access point index). An active index of 0xFF means the interface is not allocated to a client.

Revision.name: SupGetInterfaceStatusV1
Revision.Description: Get the status of one of the Piccolo interfaces (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SupGetRtsCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the capabilities of the RTS service

Revision.name: SupGetRtsCapabilitiesV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the capabilities of the RTS service (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SupGetServiceCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the capabilities of a service
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This returns the capabilities of the specified service. Each bit in the byte array determines whether a particular capability is supported. Each message exchange in the service has a capability command attribute that defines which of these capability bits it uses.
This command is only expected to be used for services that do not have their own get capabilities command (e.g. the real time service).
If the requested service does not exist, is not supported, has its own get capabilities command or does not support capabilities reporting, then this command returns a zero-length list.

Revision.name: SupGetServiceCapabilitiesV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the capabilities of a service (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SupGetServices
MessageExchange.Description: Get a list of supported Piccolo services
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This command returns a list of supported services. The services are returned in descending order of priority.

Revision.name: SupGetServicesV1
Revision.Description: Get a list of supported services (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SupGetServiceStatus
MessageExchange.Description: Get the status of the specified Piccolo service
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command returns the status of the specified Service ID. It is intended to be used to determine whether there has been an exception or the command is just taking a long time to complete.
If software suspects something is wrong (e.g. after a certain period of time the response has not been received), it can issue this command. The possible outcomes are:
(1) No response - this suggests the firmware is rebooting due to an exception and software will need to retry this command later (2) Not busy response - this suggests either the firmware rebooted due to an exception and is ready for new commands or the request was actually completed and software is mistakenly expecting more response (3) Busy response - this suggests either the request is taking a long time to complete, software should continue to wait for the response or the service has got into an undefined state, software should either wait for the firmware to (hopefully) detect this and reboot, or software should power-cycle the device itself (wired devices only)
If the SupGetServiceStatusFlagNotSupported bit indicates a pseudo-service it means the service ID byte value is used for special purposes and does not represent an actual service. Examples are the ID bytes of "not ready" packets and I2C retry ack packets.

Revision.name: SupGetServiceStatusV1
Revision.Description: Get the status of the specified Piccolo service (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SupGetSupRtsCapabilities
MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the capabilities of the supervisor and RTS services
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command is an alias of the concatenation of SupGetCapabilities and SupGetRtsCapabilities.
The supervisor service only supports basic packetization which means that normally it is not permitted to concatenate multiple commands together in a single transport packet. The purpose of this alias is to make an explicit exception for this case by making the combination appear to be a single command.
The response to this command is not documented here. It is the concatenation of the response to SupGetCapabilities and the response to SupGetRtsCapabilities. Refer to those commands for the response format.

Revision.name: SupGetSupRtsCapabilitiesV1
Revision.Description: Get a bitmap of the capabilities of the supervisor and RTS services (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SupNoOp
MessageExchange.Description: No operation command
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This command does nothing except return a null (empty) response.

Revision.name: SupNoOpV1
Revision.Description: No operation command (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SupResetServices
MessageExchange.Description: Reset all Piccolo services for this client
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command resets all services (except supervisor service) for "this" client. Resetting the supervisor service is not required as this service does not support extended packetization and is not expected to be in a "waiting state". Resetting a service means that the services returns to "idle" state and is able to accept any new request from software.
Resetting services will cause the following actions for the requesting client:
- cancel any chained Piccolo request initiated by this client - exit programming mode if it was granted to this client - close the AFS file handle if this client opened it with AfsOpenFile - stop any keep-alive messages that were being sent to this client - cancel all ENS subscriptions for this client (except the default subscriptions) - stop any data running over the Real Time Service (RTS) to this client - stop any modalities running over the Multimodal Service (MMS) to this client - stop any streams running over Isochronous Streaming Service (ISS) to this client - send a DevServicesReset to this client
Mobile apps are expected to send this command when connecting to HA device in case the previous session was not shut down cleanly.

Revision.name: SupResetServicesV1
Revision.Description: Reset all Piccolo services for this client (excluding the supervisor service) (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysAuthenticate
MessageExchange.Description: Authenticate by sending response to challenge
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command authenticates the client for memory access if the response to the previous challenge is correct. The following commands are available only when the client is authenticated:
SysWriteMemory SysReadMemory SysCheckMemory SysEraseMemory SysCopyMemory
Note that the RIC memory target is never restricted.
Authentication is only available in programming mode and is revoked when programming mode is exited. Only the requesting client is authenticated, the restricted commands will remain restricted for other clients. Attempting the restricted commands when not authenticated will cause a service exception.

Revision.name: SysAuthenticateV1
Revision.Description: Authenticate by sending response to challenge (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysBatteryStatusChanged
MessageExchange.Description: Battery status changed
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
The new battery status values at the time the event occurred are included with the event. This event is broadcast to all subscribed clients.
This event is only generated on a battery level change, not on a battery voltage change.

Revision.name: SysBatteryStatusChangedV1
Revision.Description: Battery status changed (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysCheckMemory
MessageExchange.Description: Generate a CRC checksum from the contents of memory
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command calculates the CRC checksum of a block of data in one of the memory spaces.
This is the CRC according to the CRC16-CCITT standard using the polynomial 0x1021 and an initial seed of 0xFFFF. The most significant byte is returned first.
Checking a target not listed in the response to SysGetMemoryTargets will cause an exception.
Checking a target that is not ready (e.g. the RF subsystem is disabled or de-configured) will return undefined checksum.
Checking the RIC NVM when no RIC assembly is attached will result in the RIC NVM Error status bit being set will return undefined checksum.

Revision.name: SysCheckMemoryV1
Revision.Description: Generate a CRC checksum from the contents of memory (version 1)

Revision.name: SysClearExceptionV1

MessageExchange.name: SysControlLed
MessageExchange.Description: Control LED
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
New requests that use an LED from an ongoing previous request will override the previous request. Similarly, LED control that originates elsewhere (e.g. within firmware) will also override a previous request. Additionally, a request using this message exchange will override LED control originating elsewhere.
The alternate function requires a primary and secondary LED so a new request that involves either will terminate the alternate function.

Revision.name: SysControlLedV1
Revision.Description: LED control (version 1)

Revision.name: SysControlsChangedV1
Revision.Description: System controller's programming mode control flags changed (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysCopyMemory
MessageExchange.Description: Copy memory from one area to another
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command copies data from one of the memory spaces to another (or the same). Overlapping source and target is not supported.
Copying to or from a target not listed the response to SysGetMemoryTargets will cause an exception.
Copying to target that is not ready will be ignored.
Copying from target that is not ready will cause undefined data to be copied.
Not all source and target combinations are supported, specifically only NVM (EEPRON/Flash) source and targets are supported and then BLE to BLE and NFMI to NFMI are excluded.

Revision.name: SysCopyMemoryV1
Revision.Description: Copy memory from one area to another (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysDelay
MessageExchange.Description: Delay for a specified time
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: Delays for the specified period before returning the (empty) response or executing the next command in the packet. Delay cannot be zero.

Revision.name: SysDelayV1
Revision.Description: Delay for a specified time (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysEcho
MessageExchange.Description: Echo the command payload as a response

Revision.name: SysEchoV1
Revision.Description: Echo the command payload as a response (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysEraseMemory
MessageExchange.Description: Erase memory
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command erases all memory in the specified range. For some target IDs the memory can only be erased by sector. This command will erase all sectors that encompass the specified byte range.
The erase value is target ID specific but guarantees that a subsequent write to the specified region will succeed.
Nothing is erased if the length is zero.
The sector size is target ID and platform specific.
Ezairo Flash and EEPROM are the only memory spaces that currently support the erase memory command. Attempting to erase a different memory space will cause an exception.

Revision.name: SysEraseMemoryV1
Revision.Description: Erase memory (version 1)

If "force_exit" flag is set when wireless client enters programming mode, firmware exits programming mode if the client doesn't issue any Piccolo commands on the wireless interface for the "inactivity" timeout period.

MessageExchange.name: SysGetStatus
MessageExchange.Description: Get the system controller's status
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
The shutdown bit is provided primarily for test/debug purposes because it is not expected that software will connect to an aid that has shut down. However, on a dev board without the D02 HPM10 PMIC hooked up, the system will not actually power down but normal operation will cease.
The DFU bit is provided primarily for test/debug purposes because it is not expected that software will connect to aid in DFU mode (DFU mode prevents wireless operation).
The active partition is not necessarily the same as the partition to boot as indicated by the boot pointer in NVM. Partitions can be made active temporarily without committing the boot pointer.

Revision.name: SysGetStatusV1
Revision.Description: Get the system controller's status (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysGetTimestamp
MessageExchange.Description: Get the execution timestamp
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Takes a snapshot of the firmware's internal timer and returns it as a timestamp.
The timestamp is reset to zero when the Piccolo subsystem starts after firmware reboot or reinit or by a SysResetTimestamp command. By placing a timestamp reset before a command and a get timestamp after the command (all in the same packet), an accurate command execution time can be measured.
This command only returns accurate results for elapsed times (since reset timestamp) of up to 1 hour.

Revision.name: SysGetTimestampV1
Revision.Description: Get the execution timestamp (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysGetUpTime
MessageExchange.Description: Get the amount of time the hearing aid has been running since it was last turned on
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Takes a snapshot of the firmware's internal millisecond timer and returns it as a timestamp.
The timer is reset to zero when firmware reboots or reinits.
This command returns results for up times of up to ~50 days. It is unlikely for a hearing aid to be running that long, but if it did, the timer would rollover to 0 and start counting up again.

Revision.name: SysGetUpTimeV1
Revision.Description: Get the amount of time the hearing aid has been running since it was last turned on (version 1)

MessageExchange.Description: Get a bitmap of the system visible indicator feature capabilities supported by the firmware

Revision.name: SysGetWiCrosTxBatteryStatusV1
Revision.Description: Get the WiCROS transmitter's battery status (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysNoOp
MessageExchange.Description: No operation command

Revision.name: SysNoOpV1
Revision.Description: No operation command (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysPowerOff
MessageExchange.Description: Power off the hearing aid
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
The default behavior (without setting any flags) is to power off the aid in a similar manner to the PowerOff feature ID.
Ship mode puts the hearing aid into deep sleep to minimize battery drain. May require docking/undocking from charger to power back up.

Revision.name: SysPowerOffV1
Revision.Description: Power off the hearing aid

MessageExchange.name: SysReadMemory
MessageExchange.Description: Read bytes from memory
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Ezairo CFX X and Y memory are addressed as 24 bit words, Ezairo CFX P memory and NFMI NVM as 32 bit words, and all other as bytes.
Length is always in bytes regardless of address space word size.
Reading from a target not listed in the response to SysGetMemoryTargets will cause an exception.
Reading from a target that is not ready (e.g. the RF subsystem is disabled or de-configured) will return undefined data.
Reading from the RIC NVM when no RIC assembly is attached will result in the RIC NVM Error status bit being set and will return undefined data.

Revision.name: SysReadMemoryV1
Revision.Description: Read bytes from memory (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysReboot
MessageExchange.Description: Reboot the hearing aid into the specified mode
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command does not run the ROM bootloader (unless the reboot flag is zero) but it executes both the system bootloader and the application bootloader which makes it possible to boot a different partition.
Unlike the SysReinit command, this command fully reloads the application.
If the flags and boot partition are not present, the device reboots the current committed partition into normal mode.
If the boot partition is not present, the device reboots the current committed partition.
Rebooting to a different partition doesn't make any persistent change to the boot pointer in NVM.
DFU mode is only supported in conjunction with safe mode.
See the SysReset command for the procedure to reconnect to the firmware.
The reboot flag should always be set otherwise all other arguments will be ignored and a full reset will occur.

Revision.name: SysRebootV1
Revision.Description: Reboot the hearing aid into the specified mode (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysReinit
MessageExchange.Description: Reinitialize the hearing aid into the specified memory
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This causes the application bootloader to re-execute and re-initialize the application data segments but it does not reload the read-only application segments. It does not re-execute the system bootloader.
If reinit is attempted on an uncommitted partition (where the executing firmware is not from the committed partition) then it will reboot into the committed partition (fully reloading all segments) and start in the default memory (regardless of the arguments supplied here). This scenario can happen when a reinit is attempted during a DFU before the target firmware is acknowledged.
Reinit plays the memory indicator (if ReinitIndicatorEnable is set) rather than the power-on indicator and does not delay for the PowerOnDelay period.

Revision.name: SysReinitV1
Revision.Description: Reinitialize the hearing aid into the specified memory (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysReset
MessageExchange.Description: Reset the hearing aid
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Reboot the device through a firmware-initiated hardware reset. This causes the primary and secondary bootloaders to execute as if the device had been power cycled.
This command does return a response. Approximately 250ms after the response is returned, the firmware will disconnect from the programmer and initiate the reset process.
Software should wait at least 500ms after receiving the response to this command before attempting any new commands (to ensure that the reset process has begun).
On a wired connection, software should take the response within 250ms of it becoming available, otherwise the response will be lost. Therefore software should be polling continuously faster than every 250ms. When firmware disconnects from the wired programmer, I2C transactions will be NAK'd until the firmware has come back up. A NAK means that the device will appear to be physically disconnected from the programmer. Assuming software waits for the 500ms after receiving the response to the reset command as mentioned above, all I2C transactions will be NAK'd until the firmware is ready to enable the I2C slave interface. Software can periodically poll for this by repeatedly attempting a Piccolo command until it isn't NAK'd (at which point the expected response should be available to read). This could take up to 10 seconds. If software is not prepared to handle NAK's from the programmer then it needs to wait until it can be sure the firmware is ready. The required delay is TBD but it could be 30 seconds or more, worst case.
On a wireless connection, after the response to this command is received, software should wait for 500ms or until the Bluetooth connection is dropped and then wait for the connection to be reestablished before attempting further commands.

Revision.name: SysResetV1
Revision.Description: Reset the hearing aid (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysResetDataLog
MessageExchange.Description: Reset the product data logs
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command resets the data log parameters (except the ones below) in context data files. Before resetting the data logs, a snapshot of the hearing aid on time (AidOnTime*) is saved in another LPI parameter (LastDataLogResetTime*).
AidOnTimeHours AidOnTimeSecs LastDataLogResetTimeHours LastDataLogResetTimeSecs
This command has no effect in factory mode.

Revision.name: SysResetDataLogV1
Revision.Description: Reset the product data logs (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysResetTimestamp
MessageExchange.Description: Reset the firmware execution timestamp

Revision.name: SysResetTimestampV1
Revision.Description: Reset the firmware execution timestamp (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysSetBootPartition
MessageExchange.Description: Set the partition to boot from on the next reset
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
If the partition field is set to Active partition, the partition that is running shall be written to the partition to boot.
If the partition field is set to Inactive partition, the opposite partition to the one that is running shall be written to the partition to boot. If the partition field is set to Inactive partition and if the inactive partition does not have valid firmware this will result in a bricked device on the next reboot/reset.
The preferred procedure is to first boot to the desired partition using SysReboot and then use SysSetBootPartition to the active partition. This ensures the target partition is indeed bootable.

Revision.name: SysSetBootPartitionV1
Revision.Description: Set the partition to boot from on the next reset (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysSetControlFlags
MessageExchange.Description: Set the system controller's programming mode control flags
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: "inhibit_nvm_update" does not affect any explicit NVM writes through the programming service (e.g. SysWriteMemory with an NVM target, AfsWrite, LpiSetParameters).

Revision.name: SysSetControlFlagsV1
Revision.Description: Set the system controller's programming mode control flags (version 1)

MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: The date and time is used by various logging features to timestamp records. It will only be valid if software has connected to the aid and set the date and time since the aid last powered on. Once the date and time is set, firmware will keep track of time as accurately as it can (it might drift). Accuracy can be improved if software periodically issues SysSetDateTime although this does mean there will be the slight possibility that timestamped records could appear to be out of order.

Revision.name: SysSetDateTimeV1

MessageExchange.name: SysSetTestMode
MessageExchange.Description: Set the firmware test mode
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
None of these bits should be used in normal operation. There might be unintended side-effects. They are intended for firmware and engineering test purposes only.
Fast new battery logging does not increase the speed until after the first normal logging period has elapsed after bootup (to avoid causing too much activity during the startup sequence). Fast new battery logging does not compensate the battery SoC metering (it will appear to discharge 100X faster). Also it increases the battery usage logging by a factor 100X (regardless of the fast battery usage logging settings) and does not compensate the streaming and audio power accumulators. Fast new battery logging should be used with care because it will increase the EEPROM wear by a factor of 100X.

Revision.name: SysSetTestModeV1b

Revision.EngineeringNote: Version 1b adds the fast new battery log test mode to version 1a

MessageExchange.name: SysStartVisibleIndicator
MessageExchange.Description: Start a visible indicator feature
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Issuing this command a subsequent time for the same feature while the previous is still active will result in restarting the visible indicator with the new duration. One exception is BleBondSuccess which will queue another in addition to changing the duration.
Issuing this command for a different feature while the previous is still active will either be honored (visible indicator changed) or ignored (success response with no visible indicator change), depending on if the new feature's priority (priorities are defined in requirements) is higher or lower, respectively. Issuing this command for a feature that is disabled via its LPI parameter will be ignored (success response with no visible indicator started).

Revision.name: SysStartVisibleIndicatorV1
Revision.Description: Start a visible indicator feature (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysStatusChanged
MessageExchange.Description: System controller's status changed
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: The new status value at the time the event occurred is included with the event. This event is broadcast to all subscribed clients.

Revision.name: SysStatusChangedV1
Revision.Description: System controller's status changed (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysStopVisibleIndicator
MessageExchange.Description: Stop a visible indicator feature
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: It is only possible to stop a visible indicator that is currently active. An attempt to stop a visible indicator that has not been started or is not longer active will result in the command doing nothing and returning success.

Revision.name: SysStopVisibleIndicatorV1
Revision.Description: Stop a visible indicator feature (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysWiCrosTxBatteryStatusChanged
MessageExchange.Description: WiCROS transmitter battery status changed
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: The new battery status values at the time the event occurred are included with the event. This event is broadcast to all subscribed clients.

Revision.name: SysWiCrosTxBatteryStatusChangedV1

MessageExchange.name: SysWriteAdcOffsetTrim0Channel0Drive2
MessageExchange.Description: Write to the ADC offset trim channel 0 drive 2 in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Writes the trim value to the device manufacturing data area in NVM (Ezairo EEPROM). Device data is specific to each device and preserved across firmware updates. Only manufacturing software and internal engineering tools are expected to use this command.
The trim values can be read back using the LPI AdcOffsetTrimDrive2* parameters in the CircuitCalibration group. Typically, these values are written after calibration is completed using the AudStartAdcCalibration Piccolo command and then using the results in the CalibratedAdcOffsetTrims group.
There are similar commands (with different values in the ID field) for ADC channels 0 through 3 and drives 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 but for conciseness not all of the aliases are listed here.
This does not take effect until the next memory change or memory refresh.

Revision.name: SysWriteAdcOffsetTrim0Channel0Drive2V1
Revision.Description: Write to the ADC offset trim channel 0 drive 2 in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysWriteBleMacAddress
MessageExchange.Description: Write to the Bluetooth MAC address in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Writes the Bluetooth MAC address to the device manufacturing data area in NVM (Ezairo EEPROM). Device data is specific to each device and preserved across firmware updates. Only manufacturing software and internal engineering tools are expected to use this command.
The 48-bit MAC address is a 6-byte array with the most signifcant byte first. For example, MAC address "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF" would be sent as an array of [0xAA, 0xBB, 0xCC, 0xDD, 0xEE, 0xFF] with 0xAA sent first.
Data can be read back via the LPI read-only BleRadioMacAddress parameter.
This does not take effect in the Bluetooth radio until the device is restarted (reset/reboot/reinit).

Revision.name: SysWriteBleMacAddressV1
Revision.Description: Write to the Bluetooth MAC address in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysWriteBleRecoveryMacAddress
MessageExchange.Description: Write to the Bluetooth recovery MAC address in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Writes the Bluetooth MAC address to the device manufacturing data area in NVM (Ezairo EEPROM). Device data is specific to each device and preserved across firmware updates. Only manufacturing software and internal engineering tools are expected to use this command.
The 48-bit MAC address is a 6-byte array with the most signifcant byte first. For example, MAC address "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF" would be sent as an array of [0xAA, 0xBB, 0xCC, 0xDD, 0xEE, 0xFF] with 0xAA sent first.
Data can be read back via the LPI read-only BleRadioRecoveryMacAddress parameter.
This does not take effect in the Bluetooth radio until the device is restarted (reset/reboot/reinit).

Revision.name: SysWriteBleRecoveryMacAddressV1
Revision.Description: Write to the Bluetooth MAC address in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysWriteCalibrateMicrophoneSensitivityCompleted
MessageExchange.Description: Write to the calibrate microphone sensitivity completed flag in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Writes the calibrate microphone sensitivity completed flag to the device manufacturing data area in NVM (Ezairo EEPROM). Device data is specific to each device and preserved across firmware updates. Only manufacturing software and internal engineering tools are expected to use this command.
Data can be read back via the LPI read-only CalibrateMicrophoneSensitivityCompleted parameter. It is intended to be used to indicate that the aid has been through the microphone calibration process.
This flag has no firmware behavior and therefore does not require any type of refresh or reinit to take effect.

Revision.name: SysWriteCalibrateMicrophoneSensitivityCompletedV1

MessageExchange.name: SysWriteCircuitId
MessageExchange.Description: Write to the circuit ID in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Writes the circuit ID to the device manufacturing data area in NVM (Ezairo EEPROM). Device data is specific to each device and preserved across firmware updates. Only manufacturing software and internal engineering tools are expected to use this command.
Data can be read back via the LPI read-only CircuitId parameter.
This takes effect immediately (it has no effect other than reflecting back through the LPI parameter).

Revision.name: SysWriteCircuitIdV1
Revision.Description: Write to the circuit ID in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysWriteDeviceManufacturingData
MessageExchange.Description: Write to the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Writes the specified device data to the device manufacturing data area in NVM (Ezairo EEPROM). Device data is specific to each device and preserved across firmware updates. Only manufacturing software and internal engineering tools are expected to use this command.
If the data is not fully provided (length is insufficient), the entry will not be modified.
Some device data can be read back via the corresponding LPI read-only parameter. Some data is considered secret and is not exposed via LPI.
During a transition phase, if the manufacturing data block being written is unpopulated, it will initialize the other values to defaults and set the version to the latest version understood by the running firmware.
For device manufacturing data that is exposed via LPI parameters in a cacheable group, software must be aware that this command could cause its cached values to become invalid.

Revision.name: SysWriteDeviceManufacturingDataV1
Revision.Description: Write to the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM (version 1)

MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:

MessageExchange.name: SysWriteIdentityResolvingKey
MessageExchange.Description: Write to the identity resolving key (IRK) in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Writes the identity resolving key (IRK) to the device manufacturing data area in NVM (Ezairo EEPROM). Device data is specific to each device and preserved across firmware updates. Only manufacturing software and internal engineering tools are expected to use this command.
The IRK is a 128-bit secret key used for pairing and bonding. It should be a unique true random number for every device.
This does not take effect in the Bluetooth radio until the device is restarted (reset/reboot/reinit).

Revision.name: SysWriteIdentityResolvingKeyV1
Revision.Description: Write to the identity resolving key (IRK) in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysWriteMemory
MessageExchange.Description: Write bytes to memory
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Ezairo CFX X and Y memory are addressed as 24 bit words, Ezairo CFX P memory and NFMI NVM as 32 bit words, and all other as bytes.
Length is always in bytes regardless of address space word size.
For CFX target memories, if the length is not a whole number of words, then the remaining bytes in the last word will be undefined.
For NFMI NVM target, if the length is not a whole number of words, then the remaining bytes in the last word will be preserved.
Some targets (in particular Flash) can only write successfully to areas that have been previously erased using the SysEraseMemory command.
Writing to a target not listed in the response to SysGetMemoryTargets will cause an exception.
Writing to a target that is not ready (e.g. the RF subsystem is disabled or de-configured) will be ignored.
Writing to the RIC NVM when no RIC assembly is attached will result in the RIC NVM Error status bit being set.

Revision.name: SysWriteMemoryV1
Revision.Description: Write bytes to memory (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: SysWriteNfmiDeviceId
MessageExchange.Description: Write to the NFMI device ID in the device manufacturing data block in EEPROM
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Writes the serial number to the device manufacturing data area in NVM (Ezairo EEPROM). Device data is specific to each device and preserved across firmware updates. Only manufacturing software and internal engineering tools are expected to use this command.
Only the least significant 20 bits of the ID are used.
Data can be read back via the LPI read-only NfmiDeviceId parameter.
This does not take effect in the NFMI radio until the device is restarted (reset/reboot/reinit).

Revision.name: SysWriteNfmiDeviceIdV1

The PPUK is a 128-bit secret key used for access authentication. It should be a unique true random number for every device.

MessageExchange.name: UiExecFeature
MessageExchange.Description: Execute a UI feature by feature ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Executes a feature and its associated indicator according to the current UI parameters.
The "feature_id" is as defined by the Piccolo protocol FeatureId enumerated type for feature IDs.
If the feature_id is any feature that changes or refreshes the current memory (e.g. SetMemory,IncrementMemory, RefreshMemory, etc.) then any LPI parameters associated with the destination memory will be refreshed from the appropriate contexts. An LPI parameter is considered associated with a memory if the parameter's context lists the memory's index in its MemoryIndexSequence property in the PiccoloInterface.xml file.
Only some features use the feature argument. For example change to absolute memory takes the memory index as an argument.
If a feature or indicator is already in progress, the execution is delayed until the current feature/indicator and any other queued features/indicators are complete.
If local execution is inhibited then there will be no indicator played and no GATT updates (because nothing local will be changed).
If default volume is inhibited, then features that might change to default volume (such as change memory, home memory, refresh memory) will leave the volume unchanged. This is ignored if any of the following are true: VolumeResetEnable parameter, Force Volume Reset flag in control flags, Force Default Volume flag below.
If default volume is forced, then features that might change to default volume (such as change memory, home memory, refresh memory) will definitely change to default volume.
The response is returned immediately and therefore possibly before the feature and indicator are executed. To wait for the feature (and its indicator) to complete, subscribe to ENS event UiFeatureCompleted.
If the feature being executed is any form of power-down, no further Piccolo commands should be issued but it is okay to wait for the response to this command to arrive.
Version 2 of this command returns an immediate response. The "request_id" is an 8-bit counter that increases every request and is maintained per Piccolo client. The same request ID will be returned in the ENS feature completed event (UiFeatureCompleted) associated with this request. The request ID is not valid unless the return code indicates success (zero).

Revision.name: UiExecFeatureV1
Revision.Description: Execute a UI feature by feature ID (version 1)

Revision.name: UiExecFeatureV1a
Revision.Description: Execute a UI feature by feature ID (version 1a)
Revision.EngineeringNote: Version 1a adds the ability to inhibit or force the default volume when changing memory.

Revision.name: UiExecFeatureV2
Revision.Description: Execute a UI feature by feature ID (version 2)
Revision.EngineeringNote: Version 2 adds the return code and request ID to the response

MessageExchange.name: UiExecIndicator
MessageExchange.Description: Play an indicator by indicator ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Plays an indicator as defined by the current parameters. Special use case enables are ignored but global indicators must be enabled. The indicator must be enabled in its parameters. Invalid indicator IDs are ignored.
If a feature or indicator is already in progress, the execution is delayed until the current feature/indicator and any other queued features/indicators are complete.
No flags are currently defined.
The "indicator_id" is the Piccolo protocol enumerated item ID for IndicatorIds and is identical to the LPI context ID for the indicator.
The response is returned immediately and therefore possibly before the indicator is completed. To wait for the indicator to complete, subscribe to ENS event UiIndicatorCompleted.
Version 2 of this command returns an immediate response. The request ID is an 8-bit counter that increases every request and is maintained per Piccolo client. The same request ID will be returned in the ENS feature completed event (UiIndicatorCompleted) associated with this request. The request ID is not valid unless the return code indicates success (zero).

Revision.name: UiExecIndicatorV1
Revision.Description: Play an indicator by indicator ID (version 1)

Revision.name: UiExecIndicatorV2
Revision.Description: Play an indicator by indicator ID (version 2)

MessageExchange.EngineeringNote: This event is only sent to the originator of the UiExecFeature command.

Revision.Description: Feature request for this client has completed (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: UiPostEvent
MessageExchange.Description: Post a UI event ID
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
Posts an event into the UI event processing queue along with any other events in the queue. On exit from the queue, the event is mapped to a feature and indicator according to the current UI parameters.
Excess events are discarded if the UI event processing queue is too full.
The "event_id" is as defined by the LPI enumerated type for LocalUiEvent.
If local execution is inhibited then there will be no indicator played and no GATT updates (because nothing local will be changed).
The response is returned immediately and therefore possibly before the event, feature and/or indicator are executed.

Revision.name: UiPostEventV1
Revision.Description: Post a UI event ID (version 1)

MessageExchange.name: UiSetControlFlags
MessageExchange.Description: Set the UI subsystem's programming mode control flags
MessageExchange.EngineeringNote:
This command sets or clears various UI subsystem control flags. Any controls that are changed are automatically restored to their original settings on exit from programming mode. Changes can only be made in programming mode.
Multiple flags can be set or multiple flags can be cleared in a single command (it is not possible to set and clear flags in a single command).
The length field can be set to any legal value. If it is shorter than the actual number of control flags bytes then only the flags corresponding to the sent mask bytes are affected. If it is longer than the actual number of control flags bytes then any excess mask bytes are ignored.

Revision.name: UiSetControlFlagsV1
Revision.Description: Set the UI subsystem's programming mode control flags (version 1)

Revision.name: UiSetControlFlagsV1a
Revision.Description: Set the UI subsystem's programming mode control flags (version 1a)

Revision.name: UiSetControlFlagsV1b
Revision.Description: Set the UI subsystem's programming mode control flags (version 1b)

Field.name: PpsAfsDfuPackageNvmBlockCrc
Field.Description:
32-bit CRC of the NVM block data
Excludes any residual bytes not included in the length specified in the BeginNvmBlock. Excludes the parcel CRC bytes.
Typically, this CRC can be calculated using the bytes present in the corresponding DE file.
This CRC is checked against the block data by reading it back from its NVM destination after the entire image package has been downloaded. For compressed NVM blocks note that the CRC is checked after the block is decompressed.
The 32-bit CRC is calculated according to IEEE 802-3 (polynomial of 0x04C11DB7 and seed of 0xFFFFFFFF).

Field.name: PpsAfsDfuPackageNvmBlockFlagCompressed
Field.Description:
Compression
0 = Uncompressed 1 = Compressed NVM block

Field.name: PpsAfsDfuPackageNvmBlockFlags
Field.Description: NVM block flags

Field.name: PpsAfsDfuPackageNvmBlockLength
Field.Description: Number of bytes in this NVM block (can be less than the number of bytes subsequently sent - any residual bytes are discarded)

Field.name: PpsAfsDfuPackagePackageDataCrc
Field.Description: CRC of the DFU package data

Field.name: PpsAfsDfuPackageScriptCrc
Field.Description:
32-bit CRC of the script data
Excludes any residual bytes not included in the length specified in the BeginScript. Excludes the parcel CRC bytes.
This CRC is checked against the script data by reading it back from its file destination after the entire script package has been downloaded.
The 32-bit CRC is calculated according to IEEE 802-3 (polynomial of 0x04C11DB7 and seed of 0xFFFFFFFF).

Field.name: PpsAfsDfuPackageScriptLength
Field.Description: Number of bytes in this script (can be less than the number of bytes subsequently sent - any residual bytes are discarded)

Field.name: PpsDevStatusFlagNvmWriteError
Field.Description:
NVM write error
false = No NVM write error (or has been cleared) true = NVM write error occurred (e.g. timeout waiting for NVM device to commit, or the readback of the data after write failed verification). This is occurs on writes from all sources (programming commands, internal parameter and file updates, DFU FW updates, etc.). It applies to all persistent memory targets accessed by Ezairo (Ezairo EEPRON/Flash, BLE NVM/NVR, NFMI NVM, etc.). This bit is cleared on SysClearException or if the device is restarted.

Field.name: PpsMmGetNumberOfRecordsAvailableStartingSequenceNumber
Field.Description:
Starting sequence number The sequence number to start counting records at. If Request All Available Records flag is set, this is not used as a starting sequence number. The response flag is still set based on this value though.
Examples:
- Starting sequence number = 3 and firmware contains sequence numbers 0 through 6, there would be 4 records available (records 3, 4, 5, and 6) - Starting sequence number = 232-1 and firmware contains sequence numbers 232-2, 232-1, 0, and 1, there would be 3 records available (records 232-1, 0, and 1)

Field.Description:
Fall trigger

Setting this bit to true will trigger a fall to be detected in the Emergency Management subsystem. The bit will be auto-cleared by firmware when it is handled. The fall will only be triggered when firmware is in the proper mode of operation as would be the case with firmware detecting the fall via the algorithm.

ItemDefinition.Description: Mute the microphone and set the microphone unmute volume to specified level (0-255). Also sets WiCROS transmitter to mute if not already muted, but does not impact the value the WiCROS transmitter unmute volume level.

ItemDefinition.name: PlayTestIndicator
ItemDefinition.Description: Play the test indicator

ItemDefinition.name: PowerOff
ItemDefinition.Description: Power off the hearing aid

ItemDefinition.name: PowerOffNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Power off the hearing aid (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: PowerOffRadio
ItemDefinition.Description: Power off the radio (airplane mode)

ItemDefinition.name: PowerOffRadioNoE2e

ItemDefinition.name: PowerOnRadio
ItemDefinition.Description: Re-enable BLE radio and re-init the device

ItemDefinition.name: PowerOnRadioNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Re-enable BLE radio and re-init the device (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: RefreshMemory

ItemDefinition.name: RefreshMemoryNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Refreshes the current memory (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: RejectLeaPhoneCallNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Reject an incoming Apple protocol phone call

ItemDefinition.name: RejectTerminateLeAudioPhoneCallNoE2e

ItemDefinition.name: RequestPva

ItemDefinition.name: RequestUnlockDtmfKeysNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Request unlock DTMF keys (multiple invocations of this feature are required to complete the unlock sequence)

ItemDefinition.name: RotateTinnitusAndMicVolume
ItemDefinition.Description: Analog rotary switch for tinnitus therapy level and microphone volume

ItemDefinition.name: RotateTinnitusAndMicVolumeNoE2e

ItemDefinition.name: RotateTinnitusVolumeNoE2e

ItemDefinition.name: RotateVolumeNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Analog rotary switch for microphone volume (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: RunSelfCheckDiagnostics
ItemDefinition.Description:
Run Self Check diagnostics using the specified options bitmap:
bit 0 - Check audio path (from mic, rear mic, receiver) bit 1 - Check sensors bit 2 - Check circuit (checks NVM health) bit 7 - Clear self check results (mutually exclusive with other bits)

ItemDefinition.name: SaveAccessoryStreamingVolume
ItemDefinition.Description: Save all ASB accessories current streaming volume

ItemDefinition.name: SaveAndUpdateAccessoryStreamingVolume
ItemDefinition.Description: Save all ASB accessories current streaming volume and update new volume index in ASB accessory volume control object based on new ASB accessory source type (item ID of AccessoryStreamingSourceType enumeration)

ItemDefinition.name: SaveEqualizerGainsNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Save the equalizer gains to NVM (currently only the streaming equalizer gains are saved)

ItemDefinition.name: SetAccessoryStreamingVolumeNoIndicator
ItemDefinition.Description: Set the accessory broadcast streaming volume to specified level (0 to 255), and not play any indicator

ItemDefinition.name: SetAdaptiveTuningAdaptationEnvironmentNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Set Adaptive Tuning adaptation to specified environment (item ID of AdaptiveTuningAcousticEnvironmentCategory enumeration)

ItemDefinition.name: SetAdaptiveTuningModeNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description:
Set Adaptive Tuning mode to specified settings (no E2E)
bit 0 - Activate (0=off, 1=on) bits 2:1 - Intent (see item IDs of AdaptiveTuningAcousticIntent enumeration) bit 3 - Decision (0=local decision, 1=use supplied acoustic environment) bits 7:4 - Acoustic environment (see item IDs of AdaptiveTuningAcousticEnvironmentCategory enumeration)

ItemDefinition.name: SetAshaStreamingVolumeNoIndicator

ItemDefinition.name: SetBalanceNoIndicator

ItemDefinition.name: SetBisSyncSuspended
ItemDefinition.Description: Suspends synchronization to the Broadcast Isochronous Stream (BIS) from a Auracast transmitter (no E2E) (0=do not suspend, 1=suspend) while still maintaining the synchronization to the transmitter (ie. Periodic Advertising (PA) synchronization). While suspended, the hearing aid will not stream audio sent from the Auracast transmitter.

An indicator will play based on increase or decrease from current level, except no mute/unmute indicator will be played.

ItemDefinition.Description: Start or stop the accessory broadcast streaming as specified (0=stop, 1=start)

ItemDefinition.Description: Sync tinnitus therapy level volume to opposite ear

ItemDefinition.Description: Toggles Adaptive Tuning on and off. If AdaptiveTuningDefaultAcousticIntent is supported, selected intent will be entered on toggle, otherwise Automatic intent will be entered.

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleAdaptiveTuningModeNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggles Adaptive Tuning on and off. If AdaptiveTuningDefaultAcousticIntent is supported, selected intent will be entered on toggle, otherwise Automatic intent will be entered (no E2E).

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleBisSyncSuspended
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggles suspension of synchronization to the Broadcast Isochronous Stream (BIS) from a Auracast transmitter while still maintaining the synchronization to the transmitter (ie. Periodic Advertising (PA) synchronization). While suspended, the hearing aid will not stream audio sent from the Auracast transmitter.

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleBisSyncSuspendedNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggles suspension of synchronization to the Broadcast Isochronous Stream (BIS) from a Auracast transmitter while still maintaining the synchronization to the transmitter (ie. Periodic Advertising (PA) synchronization). While suspended, the hearing aid will not stream audio sent from the Auracast transmitter. (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleBroadcastStreaming
ItemDefinition.Description: If any broadcast stream is active, will stop the stream. Otherwise, will attempt to start a broadcast stream from the broadcast device list.

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleBroadcastStreamingNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: If any broadcast stream is active, will stop the stream. Otherwise, will attempt to start a broadcast stream from the broadcast device list. (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleFavoriteMemoryNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Jumps to memory 4 if Favorite Memory state is not active or from memory 4 back to the previous memory if Favorite Memory state is active. The state of Favorite Memory will become inactive on any memory change (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleMute
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggle mute state for microphone, tinnitus therapy stimulus, and WiCROS transmitter to muted or unmuted. In the case of the mute states not being the same, if any of those three are unmuted, all will be muted.

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleMuteNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggle mute state for microphone, tinnitus therapy stimulus, and WiCROS transmitter to muted or unmuted. In the case of the mute states not being the same, if any of those three are unmuted, all will be muted. (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleMuteOutputNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggle the output mute state (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleNoiseControlNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggles noise control on and off (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleStreaming
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggles streaming on and off

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleStreamingNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggles streaming on and off (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleTinnitusNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggles tinnitus therapy on and off (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: ToggleWiCrosTxMuteNoE2e
ItemDefinition.Description: Toggle the WiCROS transmitter mute state (no E2E)

ItemDefinition.name: TriggerManualAlert

ItemDefinition.name: UnmuteSetDownTinnitusVolume

ItemDefinition.name: UnmuteSetDownVolume
ItemDefinition.Description: Unmute mic volume, set the microphone volume to specified level (0 to 255), and indicate volume down. Unmute tinnitus therapy stimulus volume and WiCROS transmitter if muted.

ItemDefinition.name: UnmuteSetUpTinnitusVolume
ItemDefinition.Description: Unmute tinnitus volume if muted, set the tinnitus volume to specified level (0 to 255), and indicate volume up. If not streaming (except WiCros), unmute microphone volume and WiCROS transmitter if muted.

ItemDefinition.name: UnmuteSetUpVolume
ItemDefinition.Description: Unmute microphone volume, set the microphone volume to specified level (0 to 255), and indicate volume up. Unmute tinnitus therapy stimulus volume and WiCROS transmitter if muted.

ItemDefinition.name: UpdateAccessoryStreamingVolume
ItemDefinition.Description: Update volume index in ASB accessory volume control object based on ASB accessory source type (item ID of AccessoryStreamingSourceType enumeration)
